hints: Identify the parameters of the binomial distribution: $n = 270$ and $p = \frac{1}{3}$.
Calculate the mean $\mu = np$ and variance $\sigma^2 = np(1 - p)$ for the normal approximation.
Apply a continuity correction to the discrete event $X \ge 100$ to get $Y \ge 99.5$.
Standardize the boundary $99.5$ using $z = \dfrac{99.5 - \mu}{\sigma}$ and find $1 - \Phi(z)$.
walkthrough:
Identify the binomial parameters and calculate the mean and variance for the approximating normal distribution:
$$X \sim \mathrm{B}\left(270, \frac{1}{3}\right)$$
$$\mu = np = 270 \times \frac{1}{3} = 90$$
$$\sigma^2 = np(1 - p) = 270 \times \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{2}{3} = 60 \implies \sigma = \sqrt{60}$$

Apply the continuity correction for the discrete event $X \ge 100$:
$$\mathrm{P}(X \ge 100) \approx \mathrm{P}(Y \ge 99.5)$$

Evaluate the upper tail probability using the standard normal table:
$$\mathrm{P}(Y \ge 99.5) = 1 - \Phi(1.226)$$
$$\Phi(1.226) \approx 0.8899$$
$$\mathrm{P}(Y \ge 99.5) = 1 - 0.8899 = 0.1101 \approx 0.110$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Set up the discrete model.
Let $X$ denote the number of days George goes swimming out of $n = 270$ days.
Since days are independent with constant probability $p = \frac{1}{3}$:
$$X \sim \mathrm{B}\left(270, \frac{1}{3}\right)$$

Step 2: Check conditions for a normal approximation.
$$np = 270 \times \frac{1}{3} = 90 > 5$$
$$n(1 - p) = 270 \times \frac{2}{3} = 180 > 5$$
Both $np$ and $n(1 - p)$ exceed $5$, so a normal approximation $Y \sim \mathrm{N}(\mu, \sigma^2)$ is valid.

Step 3: Calculate the mean and variance.
$$\mu = np = 90$$
$$\sigma^2 = np(1 - p) = 270 \times \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{2}{3} = 60$$
$$\sigma = \sqrt{60} \approx 7.74597$$

Step 4: Apply the continuity correction.
The discrete requirement is $X \ge 100$, which includes integers $100, 101, 102, \dots$
In the continuous model, the bar for $100$ extends from $99.5$ to $100.5$.
To include $100$ and all values to the right, we start from the lower boundary of that bar:
$$\mathrm{P}(X \ge 100) \approx \mathrm{P}(Y \ge 99.5)$$

Step 5: Standardize and evaluate.
$$z = \frac{99.5 - \mu}{\sigma} = \frac{99.5 - 90}{\sqrt{60}} = \frac{9.5}{7.74597} \approx 1.2264$$
From standard normal tables:
$$\Phi(1.22) = 0.8888, \quad \text{difference for } 6 = 11 \implies \Phi(1.226) \approx 0.8899$$
$$\mathrm{P}(Z \ge 1.226) = 1 - \Phi(1.226) = 1 - 0.8899 = 0.1101 \approx 0.110$$
